BTW, this type of stuff already happens without AI.

Remember Kelp DAO, Ledger’s Connect Kit and Drift? Those attacks involved social engineering, compromised infrastructure or security failures, without needing to break the underlying cryptography.

AI could make these attacks faster and easier. But it can also help us find vulnerabilities and fix them before attackers do.

That’s my point: the same capabilities can do a lot of good. We need to put them to work on defense, too.

#Uranium #Nuclear $M.CN $MYRUF
📅 October 13, 2026

Myriad is positioning for higher uranium prices. Los Altares looks like a very strategic move. 🇦🇷⚛️

The proposed acquisition adds approximately 55,000 hectares across 23 properties in Argentina’s Cerro Solo uranium district for $300,000 cash plus 1.57 million shares—roughly $1 million in upfront consideration at the deemed share price.

Why this matters:

🔹 Secure the ground before the cycle heats up. Higher uranium prices could make prospective assets more valuable and acquisitions more expensive. Myriad is locking in district-scale exploration exposure today.

🔹 Preserve cash for exploration. The modest cash component and reported low holding costs give Myriad flexibility over when and how to advance the project.

🔹 A permitting head start. Four properties already have granted mining concessions and approved environmental assessments. Seven more have approved assessments and are progressing through title registration.

🔹 More routes to upside. Los Altares adds Argentine exposure alongside Copper Mountain in Wyoming, in a country pursuing uranium self-sufficiency for its reactor fleet.

🔹 Stronger sector relationships. Green Shift joins Myriad’s shareholder register, bringing an indirect connection to its largest shareholder, Mega Uranium.

Historical drilling records offer a starting point for exploration. Potential ISR suitability still needs testing, and neighbouring deposits do not establish a resource at Los Altares.

The bullish thesis: acquire substantial uranium exploration optionality at a modest upfront cost, then work to unlock its value into a stronger uranium market.

If uranium prices move materially higher, today’s acquisition terms could look very well timed. 🚀

Disclosure: Paid partnership with Myriad Uranium. Please do your own research.

tweets.text:
most people only just discovered @Collector_Crypt and are probably wondering: what the hell is even Ripmart?

there‘s been a lot of rumors and speculation around it, but this recent livestream by @TuomHolmberg and @chrisakvn essentially says it all. so let me break it down for you:

one of the fastest growing trends in commerce right now is live shopping. Pioneered by Whatnot, and now followed by essentially every big platform: TikTok Shop, eBay Live, you name it.

think of Ripmart as the first truly onchain native version of something like Whatnot, powered by Collector Crypt's infrastructure.

why is this so exciting? a few reasons.

the UX.

as a collector, you don't rip packs on a livestream just because it's fun. you do it chasing that one grail you've always wanted. most of the time you don't hit it, that's part of the game, and you end up at home with a pile of worthless cards you never wanted and spent way too much money on.

with Collector Crypt underneath, Ripmart changes that. instant liquidity through buyback offers, just like you know from the gacha. you can immediately sell back, preserve your liquidity, and get way more runway to keep chasing the grail you actually want, while no more pile of worthless cards at home.

sounds simple, but that one feature gives collectors a 10x better experience (and likely also success rate in finding their grail). which makes choosing Ripmart over Whatnot and the rest a no brainer going forward.

then there is the onchain adoption.

the onchain part is obviously fully abstracted away. it just feels like using a slick new livestreaming and social app.

but what that means for @solana and @Collector_Crypt is massive. this is one of those rare events that could onboard hundreds of thousands, maybe millions of users onchain without them even realizing it, driven purely by their love for collectibles and a genuinely great shopping experience.

and let this sink in: every single pack ripped gets tokenized in real time through Collector Crypt's infrastructure. 

the supply of tokenized collectibles on Solana is about to explode. it brings a ton of liquidity to Collector's marketplace, better discovery, and adds an entirely new, highly sought after asset class on top: ungraded cards.

the traction this brings to CC and Solana is going to be huge. and the best part: it's fully organic and therefore sustainable, driven by an asset class people genuinely love and an experience orders of magnitude better than anything out there today.

and of course, Tuom wouldn't be Tuom if there wasn't a lot more going on behind the scenes, stuff beyond most people's imagination, that'll make sure Ripmart isn't just a nice idea but gets the adoption it deserves from day one.

but more on that later, once the time is right.

until then: Tuom mode.

From a multi-billion dollar marketplace to shutting down in 2 years.

This is what happens when you build shit you don't genuinely care about.

With endless funding and strong distribution, Blur could have become so much more. Instead it felt like the priority was chasing whatever was hot in the moment, rather than building something that lasts.

And honestly, it’s exactly that pattern that is one of the worst things for our industry. Founders like Pacman optimizing for short term extraction over long term sustainability and value don't just waste their own potential, they slow down real innovation for everyone.

The good news: the last few years filtered most of them out. The fewer of them left standing, the more bullish I am for the years ahead.

There was a decent amount of Indian hate out this weekend post the Olympic-bid announcement.  I’m not here to add to that. Just to ask a question or two.  

1) Why? Not because the Indians that come here are assholes. But because white men who may themselves have fought for this country in a way their ancestors have done going back one or two hundred years see the following: 

Some 28 year old who came here 3 years ago, from Mumbai or somewhere, get into his $65k car, perhaps with a white girlfriend, and drive away from his $250k job. 

2) is it wrong for that white dude to want to stop rampant visas for Indians?

I don’t think so. It’s not about competition or being a harder worker. It’s simpler than that. 

Do we have a country anymore or is it just a global game of labor exploitation by the mega corporations.  

If the latter, than who can blame those who want to reverse that trend and reinstate at least some level of home-country bias and favoritism for those who are native born and raised?
